title: Falcons Force Roster Put on the Market by Team Falcons
content:
Falcons Force, the CS2 academy team of Team Falcons, is now on the open market. Falcons announced on X on Tuesday that it is giving all five players and coach NaToSaphiX the space to explore their options. The academy team lasted 14 months. Its only link to the main roster came when Kyousuke had visa problems. Falcons did not say whether it will build a new academy team.

This article covers the statement, the players available, NucleonZ’s two stand-in spells and the academy’s results.

Team Falcons posted an official statement on X on Tuesday, November 3, at 21:49 CET. The organization said all roster and contract inquiries should go to Falcons directly.

Official Statement – بـيـان رسـمـي pic.twitter.com/S8C4Ifx74Z

The statement thanks the players for representing the colors of the organization. It does not say if Falcons will create a new academy team.

The news came a few hours after the main team knocked FaZe out of IEM Beijing 2026 . On Wednesday morning, Falcons beat HEROIC 2-0. They now face NAVI at 10:30 CET for a quarter-final place.

title: VCT Pacific : TenZ sort de sa retraite, T1 prépare une équipe de stars pour 2027
content:
C’est l’un des transferts les plus inattendus de cette intersaison sur VALORANT. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Tyson « TenZ » Ngo devrait reprendre sa carrière professionnelle en 2027 avec T1. Retraité depuis la fin de la saison 2024, le Canadien avait rejoint l’organisation sud-coréenne en mai dernier en tant que créateur de contenu. Mais son envie de compétition semble avoir repris le dessus. Le 21 octobre, son simple message « LFT » (Looking For Team) avait déjà enflammé les réseaux sociaux, dépassant les six millions de vues et récoltant près de 80 000 likes.

Véritable icône de VALORANT depuis les débuts du jeu, TenZ possède l’un des plus beaux palmarès de la scène compétitive. Avec Sentinels, il a notamment remporté les Masters Reykjavík en 2021, puis les Masters Madrid en 2024. Capable d’évoluer sur plusieurs rôles, l’ancien duelliste avait progressivement élargi son répertoire aux agents Controller et Initiator avant de prendre sa retraite. Sa dernière grande compétition remonte aux Champions 2024 à Séoul, même s’il avait effectué une brève apparition en Challengers avec Cubert Academy en mai 2025. Son retour chez T1 constituerait donc un événement majeur, autant sur le plan sportif que médiatique.

Et T1 ne compterait pas s’arrêter à cette seule recrue. Austin « crashies » Roberts devrait également rejoindre la formation coréenne après deux saisons chez Fnatic. L’Américain, passé auparavant par NRG, découvrirait ainsi une troisième région compétitive après les VCT Americas et EMEA. Mais la surprise pourrait surtout venir du staff, avec l’arrivée attendue de Gustavo « Sacy » Rossi au poste d’entraîneur principal. Champion du monde en 2022 avec LOUD, le Brésilien retrouverait TenZ, avec qui il avait remporté les Masters Madrid en 2024 sous les couleurs de Sentinels. Il s’agirait de sa première expérience officielle comme coach.

Cette reconstruction marquerait un changement radical pour T1, habitué à aligner un effectif exclusivement sud-coréen ces dernières saisons. L’organisation aurait décidé de se séparer de Munchkin, Meteor et DH, tandis que BuZz et stax seraient toujours en discussions pour prolonger leur aventure. iZu reste quant à lui sous contrat jusqu’en 2027. T1 devra néanmoins conserver au moins trois joueurs sud-coréens pour répondre aux exigences régionales évoquées par Sheep Esports . Après son sacre aux Masters Bangkok en 2025, la structure entend visiblement retrouver les sommets avec un projet international particulièrement ambitieux. Reste à voir si le retour de TenZ, associé à l’expérience de crashies et Sacy, permettra à T1 de franchir un nouveau cap en VCT Pacific.

title: BetBoom survive Liquid’s Nuke comeback to book a Beijing quarter-final
content:
Liquid won 12 of the last 14 rounds on Nuke from 1-9 down, but Boombl4 kept Mirage together and BetBoom took the last word.

BetBoom Team reached the quarter-finals of IEM Beijing 2026 on Wednesday with a 2-1 win over Team Liquid in the Group B lower bracket final: 13-5 on Anubis, 11-13 on Nuke and 13-11 on Mirage. Liquid are out in seventh to eighth place with $54,500, a few hours after they had knocked out TYLOO.

We showed resilience… But we know the Major will demand more of us. pic.twitter.com/lrJJM8f0nB

For a map and a half, it looked like a short afternoon. Liquid had won Anubis 13-4 twice in Beijing, against Aurora and TYLOO, and picked it again. Magnojez took it away from them. The BetBoom rifler went 21-5 with 114.5 ADR on the map, including a 1v3 on the A site, and Liquid did not win a single round on their T side.

MagnojEZ 1vs3 CLUTCH on the A-site #IEM pic.twitter.com/SB7sVro91X

BetBoom’s own Nuke pick started the same way. Boombl4 won the pistol round with a lurk and a backstab, and his side found timing after timing on the T side. Jorko kept getting caught on his way to his AWP spots, and Liquid were 1-9 down before they won two rounds to make it 3-9 at the half.

title: TenZ lines up T1 comeback with crashies, Sheep Esports reports
content:
Two years after he retired, the two-time Masters champion would move from T1’s content team into its VCT Pacific lineup, with another American beside him.

Tyson “TenZ” Ngo is set to return to professional VALORANT with T1 for the 2027 VCT season, Sheep Esports reports. According to the same outlet, Austin “crashies” Roberts is also set to join T1 after two seasons at Fnatic. Neither T1, TenZ nor crashies has confirmed the moves.

Sheep’s sources say the 25-year-old Canadian “is therefore expected to return to the server and competition in 2027”. He has been with the South Korean organisation since May, but as an influencer and content creator rather than a player.

TenZ announced his retirement from competitive play on 14 September 2024, after Sentinels finished fourth at VALORANT Champions Seoul, and moved into content creation for the organisation. It ended a VALORANT career that began at Cloud9 in 2020 and brought two Masters titles with Sentinels, in Reykjavík in 2021 and Madrid in 2024.

He has hardly played official matches since. In May 2025 he stood in for Cubert Academy, Sentinels’ academy side, in the North American Challengers playoffs. A year later, on 10 May 2026, T1 announced him as an influencer.

On 21 October he told his followers on X that he was looking for a team. The post has since passed 6 million views.

title: MOUZ crush PARIVISION 13-2 on their best map
content:
PARIVISION picked the Ancient they had won twice in Beijing and left it with two rounds, and MOUZ go straight to the semi-finals without dropping a map.

MOUZ won Group B of IEM Beijing 2026 on Wednesday morning with a 2-0 win over PARIVISION in the upper bracket final, 13-2 on Ancient and 13-9 on Mirage. MOUZ skip the quarter-finals and play their semi-final on 7 November, while PARIVISION have one more series to play on Friday.

Without losing a single map, we‘re moving from the basement to the semi finals. See you on stage 🫡 pic.twitter.com/2jDldQQYCi

Ancient was the map PARIVISION trusted most. They had won 10 of their 13 maps there over the last three months, including 13-9 against G2 and 13-7 against Liquid earlier in the event, while MOUZ had won only half of their eight. PARIVISION picked it, MOUZ let it through. It was a rout.

It started well enough for PARIVISION on the T side. They won the pistol round, and in the fourth round Abay “HObbit” Khassenov won a 1v1 against Ádám “torzsi” Torzsás with almost no health left to make it 2-2. That was the last round they won for a long time. MOUZ took the next eight to lead 10-2 at the half, and PARIVISION had used two timeouts by then.

One round summed it up. Lotan “Spinx” Giladi and PR were left 2v4 with barely any health between them, held their positions and won it. Spinx then opened the second half with four kills on the pistol round, and MOUZ added the last three rounds without reply. The Israeli finished the map 18-6 with 129.5 ADR and 100% KAST, while zweih went 1-14.

title: donk tops FACEIT’s most-reported list with 1,662 reports
content:
The Spirit star has been reported more than twice as often as anyone else from the world’s top ten teams.

Danil “ donk ” Kryshkovets is the most-reported player from the top ten teams in the Valve Regional Standings, FACEIT posted on X on Tuesday 17:49 CET . The Team Spirit rifler has received 1,662 reports over his career on the platform, more than double the 801 for Team Falcons ‘ kyousuke in second place.

Every top professional is accused of cheating on their way up. These are the most-reported pros from the top 10 VRS Ranked teams, by reports received on FACEIT during the careers that lead to the biggest LAN stages. pic.twitter.com/VatoMSBFiv

The gap at the top is the striking part. cmtry, Krabeni and molodoy have 1,525 reports between them, still 137 fewer than donk on his own.

FACEIT’s graphic describes the list as the pros “most reported for cheating and smurfing”, and the post opens with “Every top professional is accused of cheating on their way up.” A report is a complaint filed by another player in a match, not a finding, and FACEIT does not say that any of the five did anything wrong. FACEIT’s own point is that players this good draw reports in matchmaking long before they are known names.

cmtry is listed here because he still counts on FUT Esports ‘ VRS roster, even though he now plays for Astralis . His former FUT teammate dem0n, who overtook donk as FACEIT’s highest-rated player on Sunday, does not make the top five.

title: NAF aces twice as Liquid eliminate TYLOO 2-0
content:
The Canadian has now played TYLOO seven times in his career and won all seven, and his Anubis half sent the home side into the off-season.

Team Liquid knocked TYLOO out of IEM Beijing 2026 on Wednesday morning with a 2-0 win in the Group B lower bracket semi-final, holding off a late fightback on Mirage (13-11) before running away with Anubis (13-4). TYLOO finish ninth to 12th with $25,000, and Liquid play BetBoom for a quarter-final place in the morning’s second series.

Job's not finished yet… pic.twitter.com/rAHbeBznJD

Before the match, the casters called Keith “NAF” Markovic the TYLOO slayer. He met them with OpTic in 2016, twice with Renegades at the 2017 Asia Minor and three times with Liquid, and he never lost a series. A rough Mirage (10-14) did not change that, because Anubis was his.

TYLOO had lost their last four matches on Anubis, against Lynn Vision, Falcons, M80 and Spirit, and Liquid picked it for that reason. EliGE opened the CT side with four kills on the pistol round. In round five NAF held B against a full TYLOO buy, took three through Canal and then turned to mid to finish all five.

ALL FIVE FROM @NAFFLY 🦥 #IEM pic.twitter.com/vglea31zey

title: BGMI Air Launch Date Confirmed: KRAFTON India Reveals When the 1GB Game Arrives
content:
BGMI Air launches in India on Thursday, December 10, 2026, KRAFTON India announced on November 4. The lighter version of Battlegrounds Mobile India crossed 14 million pre-registrations on Google Play before a date was even announced. A closed beta comes first, from November 20 to 24 in Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata.

That’s 36 days from the announcement to launch. For millions of players whose phones couldn’t handle full BGMI, the wait finally has an end date.

December 10, 2026. KRAFTON India confirmed the date in a press release on November 4, less than three weeks after BGMI Air crossed 14 million pre-registrations on Google Play.

KRAFTON India says more pre-launch details and rewards will be shared through BGMI Air’s official social media handles before launch.

The game has moved fast since the rebrand. It reached 10 million pre-registrations soon after KRAFTON renamed BGMI Lite to BGMI Air, as we covered in our report on how BGMI Air pre-registrations crossed 10 million . It has added another 4 million since.

Around 1 GB for the initial download, according to KRAFTON India. The game is built for players whose devices or storage kept full BGMI out of reach, while keeping the core gameplay the same.

title: VCT EMEA : la Karmine Corp verrouille SUYGETSU et prépare un mercato sans changement
content:
La Karmine Corp mise sur la stabilité pour la prochaine saison des VCT EMEA. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Dmitrii « SUYGETSU » Iliushin aurait trouvé un accord avec l’organisation française pour prolonger son contrat jusqu’en 2027. Une nouvelle qui intervient au lendemain de l’officialisation de la prolongation de l’entraîneur Ahmed « ZE1SH » Sheikh, désormais lié au club jusqu’en 2028. Les autres joueurs étant déjà sous contrat pour la saison prochaine, KC devrait donc repartir avec exactement le même cinq de départ.

Arrivé fin 2024, SUYGETSU est aujourd’hui l’un des joueurs les plus anciens de l’effectif, aux côtés de Hazem « avez » Khaled. Champion des Masters Copenhague 2022 avec FunPlus Phoenix, où il avait également décroché le titre de MVP de la finale, le Russe apporte une expérience précieuse à une formation particulièrement ambitieuse. Après avoir longtemps brillé individuellement dans un rôle de Sentinel, il a accepté de prendre davantage de responsabilités dans l’ombre cette saison, laissant notamment plus de place à Marshall « N4RRATE » Massey et Burak « LêwN » Alkan.

Ce choix s’explique notamment par la spectaculaire progression de la Karmine Corp au cours de l’année 2026. Après un début de saison très compliqué, l’arrivée de ZE1SH au poste d’entraîneur principal a complètement transformé l’équipe. Portée par un système plus flexible et une meilleure liberté de jeu, KC a remporté le Stage 2 des VCT EMEA, décrochant ainsi son deuxième titre européen et sa toute première qualification pour les VALORANT Champions.

L’aventure mondiale s’est toutefois arrêtée dès la phase de groupes à Shanghai, après des défaites contre NRG et NS RedForce. Malgré cette élimination, les dirigeants semblent convaincus du potentiel de leur effectif et préfèrent miser sur les automatismes développés ces derniers mois plutôt que de procéder à une nouvelle reconstruction. Une stratégie relativement rare sur VALORANT, où les changements de joueurs sont fréquents à chaque intersaison. Reste désormais à savoir si cette stabilité permettra à la Karmine Corp de confirmer son retour au sommet européen en 2027.

title: Falcons put their whole academy roster on the market
content:
Falcons Force lasted 14 months, and their only route into the main team was a visa problem.

Team Falcons have placed their entire academy team, Falcons Force, on the open market. The organisation said in a statement on X on Tuesday 21:49 CET that it is giving the five players and coach NaToSaphiX “the space to explore their options”, and that all roster and contract enquiries should go to Falcons directly.

Official Statement – بـيـان رسـمـي pic.twitter.com/S8C4Ifx74Z

The statement thanks the players for “representing our colours” but does not say whether Falcons will build a new academy team. The announcement came a few hours after Falcons knocked FaZe out of IEM Beijing 2026 , and the main team have kept going since: on Wednesday morning they beat HEROIC 2-0 and now face NAVI at 10:30 CET for a quarter-final place.

Falcons announced NaToSaphiX as coach in July 2025 and the lineup on 15 September 2025. Olaie started as captain but was benched in February, when Norwegian IGL Tapewaare came in from Copenhagen Wolves.

NaToSaphiX picked the players himself after a long trial process, Dust2.dk reports. He came to Falcons straight from coaching NIP Impact, and the Dane played for HEROIC in 2019 before that.

title: Sentinels complete their 2027 lineup with world champion brawk
content:
A day after OXY, Sentinels have taken the 2025 Champions MVP from NRG, who are now down to three players.

Sentinels have signed Brock “brawk” Somerhalder from NRG, the organisation announced on X on Tuesday at 22:00 CET . The American initiator joins OXY, in-game leader johnqt, Reduxx and cortezia, which gives Sentinels five players for the 2027 VCT season less than 24 hours after they signed OXY from Cloud9 .

Bringing out the big guns World Champ @brawk is officially a Sentinel pic.twitter.com/G9Xhx25W2z

The signing ends a two-year run at NRG that brought the biggest title in the game. brawk was named MVP at VALORANT Champions 2025 in Paris, where NRG beat Fnatic 3-2 in the grand final.

NRG said goodbye first, two hours before Sentinels made it official, calling him a “World Champ, Odin King, and an indelible part of NRG’s legacy”. A minute later brawk explained that he had chosen not to re-sign:

This might seem like a surprise to some, but I have decided not to re-sign with NRG. This was probably one of the hardest decisions I have ever had to make in esports. […] Being a pro player sometimes requires very tough decisions and my goal as a player is to put myself in the best spots to win another trophy.

title: Liquid Beat TYLOO 2-0 at IEM Beijing 2026 as NAF Posts Career Best Map
content:
Team Liquid knocked TYLOO out of IEM Beijing 2026 on Wednesday, November 4, winning 2-0 on Mirage (13-11) and Anubis (13-4) in a Group B lower-bracket elimination match. Liquid now play BETBOOM for the last Group B place in the playoffs. TYLOO go home after one series win at their home event, and their hopes of reaching the PGL Singapore Major are now slim.

Liquid built a big lead on Mirage, then nearly threw it. They led 8-4 at half and moved to 11-4, then TYLOO won seven rounds in a row, saving four map points and pulling back to 11-12. Liquid steadied and closed the map 13-11.

Anubis was never close. Liquid went 7-0 up, led 11-1 at half and finished it 13-4.

Jonathan “EliGE” Jablonowski led the series with 43 kills to 24 deaths and a 1.67 rating, according to HLTV’s match stats. He had 25 of those kills on Mirage, where Liquid needed them most.

Keith “NAF” Markovic took over on Anubis. He finished the map with 22 kills and a 2.60 rating, the highest-rated map of his career, according to HLTV, and landed two aces in the series. Yi “JamYoung” Yang was TYLOO’s best player, with 40 kills and a 1.38 rating, but he got little support. Three of his teammates finished the series below a 0.80 rating.

TYLOO pulled out of HyperX Retake so they could play IEM Beijing in front of a home crowd. That event was one of their routes to the PGL Singapore Major, and pulling out left them likely to miss Singapore, as we covered in our report on TYLOO’s HyperX Retake forfeit .

title: DJ Sona Ultimate Remix Mythic Variant: First impressions
content:
The long-awaited Firestarter-themed skin for Sona is finally here! Unfortunately, it comes as a Mythic Variant of DJ Sona called Ultimate Remix . Here’s our first look at the skin.

Dropping club bangers and pentakills in equal measure. The Mythic Variant DJ Sona Ultimate Remix is heading to the PBE. pic.twitter.com/oK5K3t6j7V

The Mythic Variant DJ Sona Ultimate Remix will be available in League of Legends Patch 26.23 , scheduled for Nov. 18, 2026 .

You can acquire the skin through a limited-time banner in the Sanctum , and this is the first Mythic Variant for an Ultimate skin.

The base rate for the Mythic Variant skin is 0.5% per pull and is guaranteed within 40 pulls . This means that the unluckiest players will have to sink 16,000 RP , or about USD$135 , to guarantee getting the skin.

DJ Sona Ultimate Remix, like the base skin, also has three forms. Instead of Concussive and Ethereal, though, she gets K/DA and True Damage .

title: Aleksib leads NAVI past B8 and into a Falcons rematch
content:
A night after going 33-59 against FURIA, NAVI’s IGL ran Ancient, and B8 won three of the four pistol rounds but little after them.

NAVI beat B8 13-8 on Ancient and 13-11 on Dust2 in the Group A lower bracket semi-final of IEM Beijing 2026 on Wednesday morning, with their in-game leader at the front of it. B8 go home in ninth to 12th place with $25,000, and NAVI play Team Falcons for a quarter-final spot at 10:30 CET .

13:11 on Dust2. B8 fought hard, but we went harder. We move on to face Falcons later today for a playoff spot at #IEM Beijing 2026. GGWP! #navination pic.twitter.com/Z0x9RB7V3u

Aleksi “Aleksib” Virolainen came into the match with Tuesday’s defeat to FURIA still fresh. NAVI had led Nuke 9-3 at the half and lost it in overtime, and the Finn finished that series 33-59, the worst K-D on the server. He arrived at this one as one of the five lowest-rated players at the event. Before the first map he kept it simple on ESL’s broadcast: “It’s a new day now. Two games and we need to win them both.”

On NAVI’s own Ancient pick he went 18-10 with 107.0 ADR, the best on the server, and b1t added 21-9. B8 won the pistol round and raced to 5-1 on the CT side, winning fight after fight in mid. Then NAVI found the gaps, took six rounds in a row and went into the break 7-5 up.

title: Falcons finally win their own pick as kyousuke sinks HEROIC
content:
Five straight series had passed without Falcons winning the map they chose, and Dust2 broke that run behind kyousuke and four pistol rounds out of four.

Team Falcons are one series from the playoffs at IEM Beijing 2026 after a 2-0 win over HEROIC in the Group A lower bracket semi-final on Wednesday morning, 13-8 on Ancient and 13-6 on Dust2. HEROIC go out in ninth to 12th place with $25,000, and Falcons face NAVI at 10:30 CET for a quarter-final spot.

STICK TO DOING MEMES ON TWITTER! 👋 ONE DOWN, ONE MORE TO GO! 🦅 #FalconsAreHere – #IEM pic.twitter.com/GDTQ6BCuOi

On Tuesday, karrigan told HLTV that Falcons “can’t win our own map pick lately”, and the record backed him up. Since beating NIP at the Thunderpick World Championship, they had lost their own pick in five straight series, including Dust2 in overtime against both BetBoom (14-16) and Aurora (17-19).

Dust2 looked like it might go the same way. Falcons won the first five rounds on the T side, and then HEROIC drew level at 5-5 helped by two Falcons team kills. kyousuke took the last two rounds of the half on his own terms, a triple on a B retake and then four kills to make it 7-5.

After the break HEROIC won one more round. kyousuke won a 1v3 to bring up match point, and NiKo won the last duel to close it out.

title: Worlds 2026 : Invictus Gaming fait tomber Top Esports et file en demi-finales
content:
Le premier quart de finale des Worlds 2026 a tourné à l’avantage d’Invictus Gaming. Face à son rival de LPL, IG a rapidement pris les commandes de la rencontre grâce à une première manche parfaitement maîtrisée. Très inspiré dans la jungle, Wei a donné le ton, tandis que JiaQi a fait des ravages sur sa Kai’Sa, terminant la partie avec un impressionnant KDA de 10/1/10. Une entrée en matière convaincante pour Invictus Gaming, qui semblait déjà avoir trouvé la recette pour faire tomber Top Esports.

LE NIVEAU D'IG, WOOOOOW ! pic.twitter.com/VmHmj1C0g6

Mais TES a su profiter des erreurs adverses pour revenir dans la série. En grande difficulté sur Vayne, TheShy est complètement passé à côté de sa deuxième manche, conclue sur un terrible 1/6/5. Une prestation qui a largement contribué à la défaite d’IG et permis à Top Esports d’égaliser. Ce retour à 1-1 n’a toutefois pas suffi à inverser la dynamique d’une rencontre globalement dominée par Invictus Gaming.

Car derrière, IG a rapidement remis les choses au clair. Véritable homme fort de ce quart de finale, Wei a enchaîné deux prestations remarquables, d’abord sur Jayce (5/0/8), puis sur Naafiri (5/2/6). Deux performances décisives qui ont permis à son équipe de reprendre l’avantage, puis de conclure la série sur le score de 3-1. Même une interminable pause technique de près d’une heure et demie, survenue avant la quatrième manche, n’aura pas réussi à casser l’élan des joueurs d’Invictus Gaming.

Avec cette victoire, IG décroche le premier billet pour le dernier carré des Worlds 2026 et confirme ses ambitions dans la course au titre mondial. La formation chinoise connaîtra son prochain adversaire ce mercredi, à l’issue du quart de finale entre Gen.G et LYON. Un rendez-vous qui promet déjà un sacré défi, mais Invictus Gaming a prouvé face à Top Esports qu’il faudrait compter sur lui dans cette dernière ligne droite.

7 ANS PLUS TARD, INVICTUS GAMING EST DE RETOUR EN DEMI-FINALE ! ROOKIE ET THESHY SONT DE RETOUR DANS LE DERNIER CARRÉ ! pic.twitter.com/Yxr9bhBAC4

title: Genshin Impact 7.2 Patch Notes: Mitya, Valeriy, Banners, Events and Every Change in Hour of Ruin
content:
Genshin Impact Version 7.2, “Hour of Ruin”, launched on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, on all platforms, according to HoYoverse’s official Genshin Impact news page . It adds two new playable characters, the 5-star Electro catalyst user Mitya and the 4-star Electro sword user Valeriy. It also opens two new areas in eastern Snezhnaya, continues the Archon Quest and brings a set of quality-of-life changes. Every player at Adventure Rank 5 or higher gets 300 Primogems for the update maintenance.

Maintenance began at 06:00 (UTC+8) on November 4 and was expected to last five hours, as Genshin Impact announced on X . In other time zones, that works out as follows.

The pre-install was about 8 GB on PC and 3 GB on mobile with one voice-over pack, according to HoYoverse. Extra voice-over packs make the download bigger.

HoYoverse is giving 300 Primogems, worked out as 60 Primogems for each of the five hours the servers were down. To qualify, you needed to reach Adventure Rank 5 before maintenance began. The Primogems arrive by in-game mail within five hours after maintenance ends. Claim them before Version 7.2 ends, because the mail expires after 30 days.

Version 7.2 adds two Electro characters, as described in HoYoverse’s update announcement.

Mitya is built around a new reaction. She turns the party’s Superconduct reactions into Stellar-Conduct reactions, raises Stellar-Conduct DMG and stores a special energy. Her Elemental Skill deals regular Stellar-Conduct DMG to nearby enemies, scaling with that stored energy. Her Elemental Burst deals AoE Electro DMG and builds more energy.

title: Invictus Gaming eliminates TES in chaotic Worlds 2026 quarterfinal
content:
The first match to open the League of Legends 2026 World Championship Knockouts stage was a chaotic best-of-five quarterfinal between LPL representatives Invictus Gaming (IG) and Top Esports (TES). We got throws, stomps, teamfight wipes, and even an hour-long delay, but IG came out on top, 3-1.

It’s worth noting that Top Esports didn’t get the chance to field their actual top-laner, Cheng “ZUIAN” Zi-Hao, due to visa reasons . Veteran player Bai “369” Jia-Hao has been away from competitive League in 2026, but he truly stepped up for Worlds and was a pivotal player in TES making it to the top 8.

Game 1 was a masterclass from IG’s mid- and bot-lane carries. They swiftly dispatched TES by the mid-game, and the match was practically decided by then.

For a brief moment, game 2 looked like it was going to be the same. Sure, there were still mistakes and missteps from IG, and TES were punishing them, but it still appeared to be an eventual 2-0 for IG. Here is where 369 stepped up. After a teamfight, he was left as the sole TES member alive. His Renekton 1v3’d Kang “TheShy” Seung-lok’s Vayne , Yan “Wei” Yangwei’s Wukong , and Zi “JiaQi” Jiaqi’s fed Yunara to turn the tide and even the match, 1-1.

For game 3, they put TheShy back on tank duty as Ornn, and the team put Wei’s Jayce jungle in the spotlight instead. IG’s playbook this game was simple: Jayce pokes with an E-Q – Accelerated Shock Blast , and JiaQi’s Zeri mows them down with R – Lightning Crash. Since TES’ only form of sustain and mitigation was Seraphine and a measly BoRK on Yone, the poke was super effective.

There was an hour-long pause, which was revealed to be caused by an “emergent internal issue” with the tournament client. Other personalities who have access claimed that the whole Tournament Realm went down, possibly caused by a patch update that went live shortly before.

title: 1win Owner promises each CS2 Player a Rolls-Royce on winning PGL Major Singapore, BC Game’s CEO follows
content:
1win’s CS2 players have been handed the most glamorous incentive of the season, as the organisation’s owner has promised each of them a Rolls-Royce if they win the PGL Major Singapore 2026 . The offer arrived on November 3, only a day after Valve’s rankings confirmed that the team will be in Singapore later this month.

1win is the esports organisation backed by the betting brand of the same name, and its owner posts publicly under the name “Owner 1win”. He shared the message on his Telegram channel and on X on Tuesday evening, and fan accounts such as Ozzny_CS2 soon carried it across the wider Counter-Strike community.

The statement opened with news that the owner had just given UFC fighter Petr Yan a Rolls-Royce Cullinan for defending his title, a gift he had first promised in October. Straight after that, he turned to his CS2 team and said it had earned a chance to compete for the title at a Major “for the first time”.

Coming from an owner who has already rewarded this roster once this season, that line carries more weight than the usual pre-Major hype.

That earlier reward came barely a month ago, during the team’s best run of the year. On October 6, the owner announced a $100,000 bonus after 1win beat Team Spirit 2-0 at ESL Pro League Season 24, a result he said lifted the side into the world’s top 14. That win completed a 3-1 group run in which 1win lost to Team Vitality before beating G2, Legacy and Spirit, according to Valve’s match records. Aurora then knocked 1win out of the playoffs on October 9, although by that point the team had already shown that it could beat the very best.

title: Season 2 World Champion Toyz Walks Out of Taiwan Prison and Straight Onto a Deportation Flight to Hong Kong
content:
Toyz, the Taipei Assassins midlaner who won the League of Legends Season 2 World Championship in 2012, left a Taiwanese prison on November 3 and was put straight onto a flight to Hong Kong. The 34-year-old, whose real name is Kurtis Lau Wai-kin, had served more than two years of a four-year, two-month sentence for selling cannabis vape cartridges.

According to Taiwanese media reports, officers from the National Immigration Agency collected him from Changhua Prison at 8:00 am local time and escorted him to the airport. Images from the deportation, credited to the agency, showed him being led through the airport in a wool hat and dark clothes.

Taiwan’s Agency of Corrections approved his parole on October 19, and the Taiwan High Court’s Taichung Branch granted it a day later, as Central News Agency reported . Under normal rules, a paroled inmate serves the rest of the term under protective supervision in Taiwan.

In Toyz’s case, however, prosecutors replaced that supervision with deportation to Hong Kong, where he was born. The National Immigration Agency also said he will be barred from re-entering Taiwan for a set period, although reports have not specified how long that ban will last.

The deportation went ahead despite reports in January that Toyz had registered his marriage to Taiwanese influencer and entertainer Shinozaki Hsuan (篠崎泫) while behind bars. At the time, a lawyer quoted by Taiwanese media said the marriage showed family ties in Taiwan, which could work in his favour with the courts or immigration officials.

The immigration agency has now made clear that any future application to live in Taiwan as the spouse of a local resident will be reviewed strictly under the rules for Hong Kong and Macau residents. As a result, the marriage gives him no automatic way back, and any return will depend on how that review plays out.

title: T1 has assembled a Valorant powerhouse, TenZ, crashies and Sacy reportedly for VCT Pacific 2027

American initiator crashies is also on his way to the Korean organisation. On top of that, Brazilian world champion Sacy is set to take over as head coach, which would reunite him with his former Sentinels teammate.

None of the three moves has been confirmed by T1 yet. However, the reports land just days after the club officially began clearing space, announcing on November 2 that Meteor, DH and head coach KDG were leaving the team.

The headline move is TenZ, who announced his retirement from professional play on September 14, 2024, shortly after Sentinels finished fourth at Champions 2024 in Seoul. Since then, he has stayed close to the game as a content creator, and in May 2026 he even joined T1 as an influencer rather than a player.

That deal now looks like the first step of something bigger. TenZ had already hinted at a comeback when he posted that he was looking for a team . A full return with T1 would give the Pacific region one of the most recognisable players in VALORANT history. With Sentinels, he won Masters Reykjavík in 2021 and then Masters Madrid in 2024, the title that brought the organisation back to the top of the international scene.

crashies, meanwhile, would be heading to his third competitive region. The American played for NRG in the Americas before spending the last two seasons with Fnatic in EMEA, where he won VCT EMEA Stage 1 and finished runner-up at Champions 2025. Fnatic’s 2026 was far harder, though, since the team failed to reach Champions or any other international event for the first time in its history.

There is also a neat bit of history to the move. crashies began his VALORANT career with T1 back in April 2020, so this reported signing would bring him back to the organisation more than six years later. He has mainly played initiator throughout his career, although he spent time on sentinel duties towards the end of Fnatic’s 2026 campaign.

title: Faker et T1, vraiment intouchables aux Worlds ?

Je pense que cet état d’esprit collectif est la principale raison pour laquelle nous réussissons aussi bien dans ce tournoi. » Une recette qui a déjà permis au légendaire midlaner de remporter six titres mondiaux, et qui pourrait lui offrir une septième couronne cette année.

Pour poursuivre sa route vers un quatrième sacre consécutif, T1 devra toutefois se défaire d’un adversaire qui lui a déjà posé de sérieux problèmes cette saison. Caliste et ses coéquipiers abordent désormais ce quart de finale avec l’ambition de faire tomber les champions du monde en titre. En face, Faker et T1 tenteront de confirmer leur réputation d’équipe redoutable lorsque les enjeux deviennent les plus importants. Un duel qui pourrait bien constituer l’une des grandes affiches de ces Worlds 2026.

title: How to ‘Complete a Loot Radio Tower Side Op’ in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
content:
When you’re about halfway through the DMZ Orders in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , you’ll encounter a task to “Complete a Loot Radio Tower Side Op.” While this sounds simple enough, you might quickly realize that there is no “Loot Radio Tower” mission on the map, so where do you go to complete the Side Op?

Fortunately, we managed to complete this specific Side Op in MW4 DMZ , and we’ll explain exactly how to finish this DMZ Order.

With previous DMZ Orders, all you’ve had to do for missions like this one is look on the map and find a green icon labeled with the mission you’re trying to complete. However, there is no Loot Radio Tower mission labeled on any icon on the map, no matter how hard you look.

Instead, you need to head to one single spot on the map to complete this particular Side Op. Specifically, you need to go to “C6” quadrant in Hajin, which is located north of Deadtown . Here, just east of a Fire Station, you’ll see a blue radio tower that has red smoke coming off the top of it. If you don’t see red smoke, then another player has beaten you to this Side Op, so you’ll have to enter a new match to attempt it again.

When you spot the smoking radio tower, the “Loot Radio Tower” icon will appear on your map, giving you the go-ahead to complete the mission. To start, you need to climb the radio tower, which requires much more parkour than you’re used to in DMZ. You have to jump to poles, climb up ladders, and carefully make your way up the tower until you reach the top.

Once you reach the top, all you have to do is interact with the crate at the top of the tower, and it will complete the Loot Radio Tower Side Op in DMZ. You can loot the crate, which sometimes has decent loot, and after that, the DMZ Order task will be complete, and you can move on to the next one in MW4.

title: Fan offers Ubisoft €5M to revive the canceled Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake
content:
Not everyone has €5 million doing nothing in their back pocket. Even less have that kind of money to petition Ubisoft to restart development of the canceled Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake. However, that’s exactly what a fan going by the moniker @NachoRB10 has done, with the offer landing less than a year after Ubisoft pulled the plug on the project. For fans of the series, it's the most outrageous public effort yet to bring the remake back.

The pitch was posted as an open letter on X. It was also posted to the Prince of Persia community on Reddit, with the author claiming they’re not interested in any kind of financial return, no share of sales, no ownership of the IP, and no creative input. So what do they want? Simply a contact or the right department to send a formal proposal to.

The €5 million is obviously too small a figure to finish the game. Instead, it’s probably pitched more as a starting budget to test whether the game could resume at all. Any further funding would presumably have to follow terms Ubisoft sets, after a formal agreement and a viability assessment.

Before anyone gets carried away, though, it’s worth noting that the author is anonymous, and neither their identity nor their access to the money has been verified. Ubisoft also hasn't responded publicly.

title: Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang Denies She Was Fired for a Policy Violation: “It Is Not the Whole Story”
content:
Helen Chiang, who became Xbox’s first chief operating officer in July, has publicly denied claims that she was fired from Microsoft for a policy violation. In a LinkedIn post published on November 2, she said that version of events is “not accurate,” while also making clear that she has serious concerns about how her exit was handled.

Chiang left Microsoft on October 23 after 21 years at the company, barely three months after Xbox CEO Asha Sharma promoted her into the newly created COO role. Her post is the first time she has spoken publicly about the departure, and it comes after days of speculation that followed a report claiming she had been terminated over policy violations.

Chiang titled her post “Clarity is Kindness,” echoing a phrase Sharma had used in an interview with The Wall Street Journal while describing the tough decisions she was making about the future of Xbox. In the post, Chiang wrote that there had been “speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft,” including claims that she was “fired for a policy violation,” and added that “silence should not be mistaken for agreement.”

The original claim came from Eurogamer, which reported shortly after her exit that she had been terminated for policy violations, citing a single source. The outlet said it could not find further sources to corroborate the report, and it did not say which policy had supposedly been broken.

Chiang did not explain what actually happened, although she made it plain that the reports had left something important out. “This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story,” she wrote, adding that she wanted to set the record straight on what she called an inaccurate story about her departure.

Rather than share details, Chiang listed the explanations she wanted to rule out. She said she did not leak confidential company information to the press, and that she did not leave Xbox to join a competitor, writing that her “end game was always to keep building here.”

title: Valve Wins Hearts Once Again as Steam Support Story Resurfaces on Social Media

In a heartwarming example of customer service that has gone viral once again, Steam Support fully restored a player’s deleted game library after the user contacted them for help following periods of mental health struggles.

In the incident that originally happened a year ago, a Steam user had permanently removed numerous games from their Steam library during manic-depressive episodes. Permanent removals on Steam can’t be refunded, and users generally have no way to undo them on their own, so the player assumed the games were gone for good.

Once they were feeling better, the user wrote to Steam Support anyway. They explained what had happened, being open about their mental health, and asked whether any of the games could be brought back. If that wasn’t possible, they hoped to at least get a list of what they’d owned, so they’d know what they had lost.

Steam Support responded within a day. An agent acknowledged the player’s circumstances and restored their entire Steam library , while also offering further help if the user still needed a full list of previously owned titles.

title: PGL Cluj-Napoca 2027 Open Qualifiers Are Live: Every European Team Gets a Shot at $1.3 Million

The tournament returns to Romania from February 11 to 21, 2027, with $1,300,000 in total rewards on the line, and the qualifying road starts in just a week.

According to PGL’s announcement on November 3, two Open Qualifiers will run between November 10 and 13. Each one sends a single team to the European Closed Qualifier, where the last two places at the event will be decided from November 15 to 18.

The first Open Qualifier takes place on November 10 and 11, followed by the second on November 12 and 13. Teams sign up through FRAGNET for Open Qualifier #1 and Open Qualifier #2 , and PGL says places are handed out on a first-come, first-served basis, so teams that wait too long could find the brackets full.

Both qualifiers use a single-elimination bracket, with check-in opening one hour before the start. Early rounds are played as best-of-ones, and the series switch to best-of-three from the quarterfinals onwards. PGL has also asked every team to read its 2027 rulebook before signing up.

For smaller European rosters, these brackets are one of the few routes onto a tier-one stage that does not depend on ranking points. That makes next week a big one for academy sides, mix teams and up-and-coming organisations hoping to break through.

PGL’s 2027 rulebook sets a few firm requirements for Open Qualifier teams. Every player and coach must be at least 14 years old, a team’s region is decided by the citizenship of the majority of its players, and only one team per organisation can enter. title: GTA 6 Fan Jerry Fort Dies Three Weeks Before Launch, Months After His Viral Wish to Play It
content:
Jerry Fort, the 25-year-old TikTok creator known as Void Only, has died. He went viral in August with a video from an intensive care bed, saying he just wanted to live long enough to play Grand Theft Auto VI. His family said in a video posted to his TikTok account on November 2 that he passed away on October 29, less than a month before the game’s November 19 launch.

The news spread quickly through the GTA community, and by the evening of November 2 his name was trending on X. Rockstar Games and its parent company Take-Two Interactive have not commented publicly on his death, although many fans have since called on the studio to honour him in some way.

Fort first caught the attention of the wider gaming world on August 8, when he posted a TikTok from his hospital bed with the caption “I just want to play GTA VI. Rockstar and their delays, man.” The line struck a chord with players who had watched the game slip twice, first from its original fall 2025 window to May 26, 2026, and then to November 19, as our GTA 6 release date guide tracks.

Within days, the clip had picked up millions of views, and fan accounts on X were sharing it widely. Coverage soon followed in countries from France and Germany to Japan and Brazil, turning a personal post about a long illness into a story followed well beyond the GTA community.

In his own videos, Fort spoke openly about how serious his condition had become. He said his lungs “can’t do it no more” and that he was “at the end of my ropes.” He also explained that his lungs were attached to his chest wall, which would make the transplant surgery “very bloody, very dangerous.” Even so, he stayed hopeful, saying of his doctors that “they believe I will make it out the other side,” and he told followers he planned to stream GTA 6 once he recovered.

On the same day as his viral video, his mother, Paris Fort, set up a GoFundMe campaign from Jacksonville, Florida. Titled “Help my son reach his lung transplant,” the page says he had been battling interstitial lung disease since he was 17, and it set an initial goal of $15,000 to support his care.

title: NS RedForce Star Hyunbin Goes Straight Back to PUBG Mobile Grind After 12-Hour Trip From BMIC 2026
content:
NS RedForce won BMIC 2026 at the Dome, SVP Indoor Stadium in Mumbai on November 1, and after a 12-hour trip home to South Korea, Hyunbin went straight back to PUBG Mobile. NS RedForce head coach Janchi shared a photo on his Instagram story of Hyunbin at his desk in the team house, phone in hand.

“12 hours from Mumbai to our team house in Korea and Hyunbin is already gaming,” Janchi wrote. “He said he was just going to set up his gear. This guy is a different breed.”

Hyunbin is Jeon Hyun-bin, a South Korean PUBG Mobile player who joined NS RedForce on January 22, 2026. Before that, he spent about a year and a half at DRX, having moved there in June 2024 after a six-month spell at DUKSAN Esports.

Indian fans already knew his name. He was the MVP of BMIC 2025 in Delhi, where DRX won the title and he recorded 44 finishes across 18 matches. He then won PUBG Mobile Pro Series 2026 Season 1 (PMPS 2026 S1) with NS RedForce in May, and took the MVP award there too.

So he arrived in Mumbai as the defending BMIC MVP in a different jersey, and by the end of the weekend he had the trophy in his hands once again.

NS RedForce produced one of the most one-sided final days in BMIC’s short history. After two days, they and Dplus KIA were locked together at the top on 100 and 99 points, but NS RedForce then scored 133 points across the last six matches, won three of them and finished 82 points clear of the field.

title: GTA 6 Pre-Load Starts November 12, and Your PS5 May Need 210GB Free
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI is now 16 days from launch, and the final stretch has turned from waiting into planning. Rockstar Games has confirmed that pre-loading opens on November 12, a week before the November 19 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Meanwhile, a widely shared PS5 data tracker has put the download at 210GB, and boxed copies will not include a disc at all. Out on the streets, Miami has been dressed up as Vice City for weeks. At the same time, the community is mourning Jerry Fort, the fan who went viral in August with his hope of living long enough to play the game.

According to Rockstar’s support page on editions and versions , pre-load “will begin at local midnight on November 12, 2026” for anyone who has bought the game digitally. The US PlayStation Store listing shows a seven-day pre-load for both editions and an unlock time of 05:00 UTC on November 19. That works out to midnight Eastern, or 9pm Pacific on November 18, although other regional stores may list different times, so players outside the US are better off checking their own listing.

Pricing has not moved since pre-orders opened in June, either. The Standard Edition costs $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition $99.99, and every copy bought before November 20 comes with the Vintage Vice City Pack, while digital pre-orders also add a month of GTA+. Our GTA 6 release date guide has the full breakdown of editions and launch timing.

Anyone planning to buy a boxed copy should know that it will not save them a download. Rockstar’s support page states plainly that “A disc will not be included in the box,” and the physical version holds a download code instead. Those boxed copies are due at retailers from November 12, which Rockstar says is timed to support pre-loading, so code holders can start downloading on the same day as digital buyers.

There is also no physical Ultimate Edition, although Standard owners can still buy the upgrade later through the PlayStation Store or Microsoft Store, where Xbox currently lists it at $20.

The 210GB figure that has dominated countdown chatter comes from PlayStation Game Size, a fan-run X account that tracks PS5 store data. It posted the size for the Standard Edition on October 27, and the post has since passed 36,000 likes.

title: KRAFTON Bets on Bengaluru for Its Next Global Hit and Eyes Another Indian Studio Buyout
content:
KRAFTON wants its next global franchise to come out of India, and it is prepared to buy its way there if needed. In an interview with Bloomberg published on November 3, KRAFTON India CEO Sean Hyunil Sohn said the company plans to develop new games beyond PUBG from its Bengaluru team. He also said KRAFTON is considering the acquisition of another Indian studio, which would add to a run of investments that has already made India one of the publisher’s five largest markets by revenue.

Sohn described India’s growing profile in gaming as a major advantage for the company, and the most concrete part of the plan is about people rather than money. According to the interview, KRAFTON’s development team in Bengaluru could grow to as many as 50 people over the next two years. That signals a clear shift in what the South Korean publisher expects its Indian operation to produce.

For years, much of the work that global publishers sent to India centred on testing, localisation and art support. KRAFTON now wants its Bengaluru team, based in the country’s biggest technology hub, to build games of its own instead. Artificial intelligence is expected to play a large part in that work, since the company has publicly committed to becoming an “AI first” developer. It has already shown off PUBG Ally, a co-playable AI teammate built with NVIDIA’s ACE technology, which we covered when KRAFTON’s PUBG AI tests put Claude’s cost at $7.10 per match .

The ambition behind that shift is to find a hit that does not depend on PUBG. Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) has passed 260 million downloads and remains KRAFTON’s biggest product in the country. Even so, it is a single franchise in a market where rivals are pushing harder, as our report on how Garena is finally challenging KRAFTON in India’s mobile esports race showed.

That reliance has carried real risk before. BGMI was blocked in India in July 2022 and only returned in May 2023, initially under a three-month trial approval. KRAFTON spent much of that period rebuilding trust with regulators and players before the game recovered its place at the top of Indian mobile esports. The episode goes some way to explaining why the company now wants more than one pillar in the country.

Sohn did not name a target, a price or a timeline for the acquisition, although KRAFTON has done this once before. In March 2025, it paid $14 million in cash for a controlling stake of more than 75% in Pune-based Nautilus Mobile , the studio behind the Real Cricket franchise. The series runs to five titles, including Real Cricket 24 and Real Cricket Premier League, and the deal gave KRAFTON a homegrown sports title with a large local following alongside BGMI.

title: Is Sony Really Paying $400 for Your Used PS5? Here’s What’s Behind the Viral Offer
content:
A message promising PlayStation 5 owners up to $400 for their consoles has spread quickly online this week, and with Grand Theft Auto VI now just over two weeks away, it has helped put “PlayStation 5” among Google’s trending searches in the US. However, the offer is not quite the Sony buyback that some headlines suggest, because the money comes from Back Market, the refurbished-electronics marketplace that runs PlayStation’s trade-in programme in the US.

The promotion began circulating on November 2, when PS5 owners started sharing a message headlined “Get up to $400 when you trade in,” which names Back Market as the trade-in partner and promises a cash payment into the owner’s bank account. One of the earliest posts to spread on X came from user Knoebelbroet, who shared a screenshot of the message alongside a link to a forum thread discussing it.

Sony reportedly offers costumers up to $400 if they trade in their PS5. https://t.co/qcoYoA10CK pic.twitter.com/zltUpwtmoI

That distinction matters, since Sony itself is not buying back hardware. Back Market’s own buyback pages currently list offers of up to $415 for a standard PS5 with a disc drive and up to $385 for the Digital Edition, with quotes drawn from a network of more than 250 refurbishers. Owners get a quote online, then have 21 days to wipe their data and post the console using free, insured shipping, and the payment arrives by direct deposit within five business days.

Those top figures are maximums rather than flat rates, though, and reports on the message say the full $400 is tied to a disc-drive PS5 in pristine condition with two controllers, so any wear, missing accessories or a Digital Edition will bring the payout down. Sony has not issued a statement about the promotion, and we could not find any announcement of it on the PlayStation Blog or PlayStation Direct.

In fact, the trade-in page on PlayStation Direct still describes a PS4-only programme, in which Back Market pays for an old PS4 and PlayStation adds a $50 voucher toward a PS5, PS5 Pro or PS VR2 bought on its store. That voucher is open to US residents only, and the page lists it as valid until October 31, 2026, unless the voucher email states otherwise.

title: Masters Santiago MVP Dambi Leaves Nongshim RedForce and Hits Free Agency
content:
Nongshim RedForce have officially closed the chapter on Lee “Dambi” Hyuk-gyu, the 20-year-old Neon specialist who carried the South Korean side from the Ascension pathway to a Masters trophy in under 18 months. The organisation confirmed on November 3 that its journey with Dambi had come to an end, releasing a 15-minute farewell video titled “Thank you, Dambi” on its VALORANT YouTube channel, which passed 5,000 views within its first hour.

In the video’s description, NS traced his time with the team from its first steps on the Pacific stage to lifting the Masters trophy and fighting through Champions, and wrote that through every high and low “he always put the team first.” The organisation also thanked him for his performances and selfless plays, and said it would be cheering him on wherever his journey takes him next.

Dambi’s route to the top was anything but straightforward. Born in June 2006, he came up through Korean tier-two VALORANT with Our Growth Story and Gwangju Shadow before joining Sin Prisa Gaming in December 2023, and it was with that roster that he won VALORANT Challengers Korea Split 2 in July 2024 and then VCT Ascension Pacific in September 2024. Nongshim RedForce acquired Sin Prisa’s place in the league that November, so Dambi arrived in VCT Pacific under the NS banner alongside Francis and Ivy, who joined the organisation on the same day.

The first year in the league was a struggle, however, and NS were sent back to Ascension Pacific in 2025 and had to earn their place in VCT Pacific a second time, which made what came next even harder to predict.

The 2026 season turned out to be the best in the organisation’s VALORANT history. NS topped the VCT Pacific Kickoff in February to qualify for Masters Santiago as the region’s first seed, and in Chile they went through the event unbeaten, dropping just one map before sweeping Paper Rex 3-0 in the grand final on March 15. Dambi, who played Neon in the overwhelming majority of his rounds, was named MVP of the event, and the title made NS the first team from the Ascension pathway to win an international VCT event.

The rest of the year brought more highs and a few painful near-misses, as NS finished seventh-to-eighth in Pacific Stage 1, took third place at the Esports World Cup, and reached the Pacific Stage 2 grand final in Busan, where they led Global Esports 2-0 before losing 3-2. At Valorant Champions in Shanghai, they beat Xi Lai Gaming 2-0 in the group stage to reach the playoffs, but a 2-1 loss to Team Vitality in the upper-bracket quarterfinals sent them down a path that ended in seventh-to-eighth place.

title: CEGC 2026 Day 1 Stream Slammed by Fans as Skyesports Admits It Has No BGMI Observer Client
content:
The Chennai Esports Global Championship (CEGC) 2026 opened its BGMI group stage on November 3, yet much of the talk on Day 1 centred on the broadcast rather than the matches, after Skyesports founder and CEO Shiva Nandy publicly acknowledged the limits of what his team could put on screen. Posting on X at 2:49 PM IST, while the day’s matches were under way, Nandy wrote that without the Observer Client and API, the stream fans were watching was “the extent of what we can deliver.”

Without the Observer Client and API, This is the extent of what we can deliver.

The screenshot below is from Group A, Match 2 on Erangel. Instead of observer-driven camera work, viewers saw what was essentially BGMI’s standard in-game spectator screen, complete with the player and team counters in the top-left corner, the regular compass and minimap, and textures that looked closer to a low graphics preset than to a tournament feed. Skyesports had added its own layer on top, including a CEGC match card in the bottom-left corner and a team table on the right that tracked kills and players alive for each squad; however, the picture underneath remained the same view a player gets while spectating a friend.

An observer client is a dedicated spectator build of the game that tournament productions use to run their broadcast. It gives observers free cameras, quick switching between players and squads and cleaner visuals, while the API feeds live match data, such as kills, knocks and team status, straight into the on-screen graphics. For BGMI, organisers normally receive both from KRAFTON, and without them a production has to fall back on regular in-game spectating and gather its live stats separately, which is exactly the trade-off Nandy described.

The timing also made the gap hard for fans to ignore, because the BGMI International Cup (BMIC) 2026 , KRAFTON’s own international event, finished in Mumbai on November 1, only two days before CEGC began. Many of the viewers who tuned in to Chennai’s group stage on Tuesday had therefore spent the weekend watching a full-scale official production.

Graphics were the most common complaint in the replies. One fan said the current game and stream quality was simply bad, another asked whether the game was running on a “balanced” graphics preset, and a third argued that the commentary had also lacked energy and enthusiasm. A Hindi-language reply claimed that only two spectators were being used for the broadcast, and asked Skyesports to at least give them better phones, pointing to the backing the event receives from the Tamil Nadu government.

title: Modern Warfare 4 Review Roundup: Players Love the Campaign, Hate the Lobbies
content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has been on sale since 23 October, and the people playing it agree far more about one half of the game than the other. The campaign, which digital pre-order owners could start a week early on 16 October, has been welcomed as one of the best the series has produced. Multiplayer is a different conversation altogether, and most of the anger on Steam traces back to skill-based matchmaking, spawns and a launch map pool that few players are excited about.

We have not reviewed Modern Warfare 4 ourselves, so this roundup leans on what can be measured: Steam’s own review history, critic scores and the patch notes Infinity Ward has published since launch. The game costs $69.99 on Steam , or ₹4,999 in India, and it is out on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Nintendo Switch 2, with no version for PS4 or Xbox One. Infinity Ward leads development, while Beenox handled the PC version and Digital Legends built the Switch 2 edition , with Treyarch, Sledgehammer Games and Raven Software in support.

The Steam numbers show how quickly the mood changed. During the early access week, when only the story was playable, players left 5,238 positive reviews and 596 negative ones, so roughly nine in ten recommended it. Once multiplayer and DMZ opened on 23 October, however, the picture shifted. Since then the game has collected 3,137 positive and 2,244 negative reviews across all languages, a positive share of 58%, and the daily figure has stayed between roughly 48% and 64% the whole time. Across both periods it sits at 75% positive, while the English score on the store page reads Mostly Positive, with 73% of 5,738 reviews in favour as of 3 November.

That drop needs some context, though, because Modern Warfare 4 is still the best-received new Call of Duty on Steam in a long while. Its 73% among English reviews is ahead of Vanguard at 67%, Modern Warfare III at 46%, Modern Warfare II at 43%, Black Ops 6 at 42% and Black Ops 7 at 35%, and you have to go back to Black Ops III in 2015, which now sits at 90%, to find a yearly release that scores higher on the same store. Critics have been kinder still, with Metacritic listing the game at 85 overall, the PC version at 85, PS5 at 83 and Switch 2 at 86. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma went as far as calling it “one of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history” when she announced that the series had passed $40 billion in lifetime revenue .

Modern Warfare 4 closes out the rebooted Modern Warfare series that began in 2019, and it opens with North Korea invading the South. Much of the early story follows Private Park Hyun-jun, a young South Korean soldier whose squad is trying to hold the city of Hajin, while a second thread picks up where Modern Warfare III left off. Task Force 141 has broken up and Captain Price is on the run, with Ghost and Gaz under orders to bring him in. Price, meanwhile, is working off the books alongside Valeria Garza of the Las Almas Cartel, chasing a weapon on its way to a villain known as the Archer, played by Mads Mikkelsen, and CIA station chief Kate Laswell is still in touch with him.

Over 16 missions the story travels from Hajin to a New York nightclub, a car chase through Paris and a night raid in Mumbai, where Price and Gaz split into two teams. Mumbai later returns as one of the 12 core multiplayer maps, and one early mission even puts players in the boots of a North Korean soldier hunting a defector. Most players say they finished on Normal in six to eight hours, and anyone who beats it on Realism unlocks YOLO mode , a one-life difficulty that sends you back to the first mission the moment you die.

title: A Prince of Persia Fan Just Offered Ubisoft €5 Million to Bring the Sands of Time Remake Back From the Dead
content:
Nine months after Ubisoft pulled the plug on it, the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake has found the most unlikely lifeline imaginable, because one fan is now offering to pay for it. In an open letter posted on X on October 29, user @NachoRB10 put more than €5 million on the table to help restart development on the cancelled project, and perhaps the most surprising part is that the offer asks for almost nothing in return.

The letter, which quickly made its way to the Prince of Persia community on Reddit, goes out of its way to spell out what the fan does not want. There is no request for a financial return, no claim on a share of sales revenue, no stake in the intellectual property and no demand for any say over the game’s creative direction. Instead, the author leaves the question of whether to resume work entirely with Ubisoft, and simply asks the company to share a point of contact or direct them to the right department so that a formal proposal can be submitted.

Before anyone starts picturing a finished remake landing on store shelves next year, it helps to read the fine print, since the author is careful not to oversell the gesture. The sum is not presented as the full cost of completing the game; rather, it is framed as an initial budget that would allow Ubisoft to evaluate whether resuming development is feasible at all, with any money changing hands only after a formal agreement and a proper viability assessment, and on terms that Ubisoft itself would set.

That framing is smarter than it might first appear, because a vague promise to “fund the game” would have been easy to wave away, whereas an offer to underwrite a feasibility study gives Ubisoft something small, specific and low-risk to consider. Even so, the distance between a feasibility budget and a shippable AAA remake is enormous, and that distance is exactly where this story starts to get complicated.

The remake was officially killed on January 21, 2026, when Ubisoft unveiled a sweeping company reset that split its studios into five genre-focused “Creative Houses” and trimmed its development pipeline hard. Six games were cancelled outright, although The Sands of Time remake was the only one Ubisoft named publicly, with the rest made up of four unannounced projects, three of them new IPs, and a mobile title. Furthermore, seven other games were delayed, and the publisher confirmed the closure of its studios in Stockholm and Halifax as part of the same overhaul.

On the same day, the development team explained the decision in an official statement to the community, opening with a blunt “We know this is deeply disappointing.” According to the team, the project had potential but had not reached the level of quality that fans expected, and getting it there would have demanded more time and investment than the company could responsibly commit. Ubisoft never put a figure on that additional cost; however, the team was quick to stress that walking away from this remake did not mean walking away from the franchise.

title: 100 Thieves earn third Major sticker without playing a Major match
content:

100 Thieves entered Counter-Strike in December 2017 by signing the former Immortals lineup, which had finished second at the Kraków Major that summer and held a Legends place for Boston. On 12 January 2018 the organisation pulled out of the ELEAGUE Major Boston, citing “immigration issues”, and a team from the New Challengers Stage took the place instead. Valve still made a 100 Thieves sticker for Boston. By the end of January the organisation had released the whole squad without playing a single official match.

The second attempt came in October 2019, when 100 Thieves bought the Renegades roster that had reached the semi-finals of the StarLadder Major in Berlin. Then COVID-19 arrived. ESL One Rio was first moved and then cancelled in September 2020, and 100 Thieves left Counter-Strike again a month later. Valve still released stickers for the teams that would have been there, and the 100 Thieves sticker is in the 2020 RMR collection.

The current team, built around device and rain with gla1ve as coach, should finally end the run. Between them, device and rain have won five Majors. The organisation has not.

100 Thieves start in Stage 1 in Singapore on 24 November.

title: Understanding the Modern Gaming Ecosystem
content:
The evolution of online gaming has turned gaming into something that goes well beyond simply playing video games. There is a whole complex system of industries, companies, communities, digital economies and technology that is interacting with each other, and all of which constantly extends the meaning of a game.

Internet gaming has played a big role in this transformation. Connection has turned individual or local experiences into shared spaces where millions can play, compete, cooperate, create content and build communities.

From this inter-connectedness developed new domains like e-sports, streaming, in-game economies, and innumerable digital platforms and services. And all the while mobile and cloud computing technology has changed this world, and is forcing it to evolve.

Before the time when connecting to players all over the world became a simple matter, multiplayer gaming required a lot more work.

LAN parties became one of the first major social events for PC gaming. Games like Quake, StarCraft, Doom and Counter-Strike gathered particularly active communities there. They required lugging along a heavy desktop machine, a monitor, a keyboard and a jumble of cables to a friend’s house, a university, or an event just to be able to play for a few hours.

A LAN connection allowed several players to play the same game together without the need for outside help. The growth of the internet gradually eliminated the need for players to be in the same physical location, laying the groundwork for competitive online gaming, esports, and global gaming communities.

title: New No. 1 FURIA face NAVI for a Beijing playoff place
content:
The Bucharest champions lead HLTV’s ranking, but Valve’s standings still have them third, and NAVI beat them 2-0 only nine days ago.

FURIA are the best team in the world, according to HLTV’s ranking published on Monday, and their first test as No. 1 is NAVI in the Group A upper bracket semi-final at IEM Beijing 2026 at 10:30 CET . The winner is through to the playoffs. The loser drops into the lower bracket, one defeat from going home.

title: How to Build a Color-Themed CS2 Inventory Without Overspending
content:
Building a CS2 inventory around one colour does not have to cost a huge amount. The game offers enough weapon finishes to combine cheaper skins across rifles, pistols, SMGs, and other slots while keeping the loadout consistent. The trick is to work with shades of the chosen colour and compare wear levels. A Field-Tested or Minimal Wear skin can fit the theme just as well as a costly Factory New version. Here we explain how to choose matching skins, compare their condition and complete the loadout without overspending.

Set a budget before heading to the market. Also, decide whether you want just skins or if you’re interested in stickers, knives, and gloves as well. While stickers aren’t usually very expensive, knives and gloves require a significant investment.

Begin with weapons you use regularly. An AK-47, one M4, an AWP, Glock-18, and USP-S or P2000 appear more often than shotguns and heavy weapons. Give these slots most of the money. You can purchase skins for other weapons later. You can also find suitable stickers, charms, or additional skins for the assembled color collections later.

A theme comes from repeated colours, not a perfect match. Red and black, blue and grey, or white and black allow more choice than a single-colour rule.

A red loadout can begin with Glock-18 | Candy Apple and Galil AR | Signal, using dark skins whenever brighter red options cost too much. USP-S | Ticket to Hell fits its black side. Red stickers can tie in another dark weapon.

For blue, include navy, cyan, and turquoise. MP7 | Cirrus and P250 | Valence use different shades but still look related. Map lighting changes how colours appear, making small differences less obvious during play.
