title: Sachin Tendulkar Invests in Hitwicket Maker Metasports Interactive
content:
Sachin Tendulkar has become a strategic investor in Metasports Interactive, the Hyderabad-based company behind the cricket strategy game Hitwicket . The deal was announced on 3 November, and although neither side has disclosed how much Tendulkar has put in, the company has set a clear target, it wants Hitwicket to reach 100 million downloads within the next three years.

Tendulkar’s role goes beyond the money. He will also appear across Hitwicket’s in-game experiences, its content and its brand campaigns, which gives the game one of the most recognisable faces in world cricket at a time when it is trying to grow well beyond India.

Founded by Kashyap Reddy and Keerti Singh, Metasports Interactive launched Hitwicket in 2020, and the game now has more than 20 million players across 120 countries. Hitwicket is a competitive multiplayer game built around strategic decisions rather than reflexes, so players win by reading a match and choosing the right approach for each ball instead of by timing their shots. That focus appears to be keeping players hooked, since the company says they spend an average of 51 minutes a day in the game, and its revenue has doubled over the past six months.

Sachin says, “the game goes beyond reflexes to recreate how a cricketer thinks in the middle.”

The new investment also follows a large funding round earlier this year.

In April 2026, London-based Metica provided Metasports with $20 million in user acquisition funding, a non-dilutive model in which the company keeps its equity and repays the money based on performance measures such as user growth and revenue efficiency. At the time, Hitwicket had just over 18 million users in 109 countries, which means it has added roughly two million players and 11 countries in about six months. According to Metasports, Hitwicket’s monetisation, retention and the quality of its user acquisition data were what convinced Metica to deploy capital at that scale.

title: Intel has lost almost 50% of its value in a few weeks, as AI rout spreads
content:
Intel beat Wall Street’s forecasts on 29 October, reporting its fastest data centre growth in 15 years, and within two trading days it had lost more than a third of its market value. The shares fell almost 29% on Friday 30 October, their worst day since 1974, and then slid another 8.8% on Monday to close at $59.97. That leaves Intel worth roughly half of what it was at the end of September, and the selling has carried on well after the first shock of the forecast.

Moreover, the damage is no longer confined to Intel. Chip and memory stocks have now lost about $3.7 trillion in combined market value since 6 October, according to Yahoo Finance calculations, and the selling deepened on Monday even though most of the wider US market rose.

On paper, the quarter gave investors little to complain about. According to Intel’s third-quarter results , revenue rose 21% from a year earlier to $16.5 billion, and adjusted earnings more than doubled to 52 cents a share, comfortably ahead of the roughly 40 cents analysts had pencilled in. Adjusted gross margin improved by four percentage points to 44.1%, a sign that Intel is keeping more of every dollar it earns.

The standout was the Data Center and AI division, whose revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion as demand for server processors in AI workloads continued to climb. Chief financial officer David Zinsner described it as the strongest data centre revenue growth the company had seen in 15 years. Intel Foundry, the contract manufacturing business at the heart of chief executive Lip-Bu Tan’s turnaround plan, grew 58% to $6.7 billion. The one weak spot was the PC business, now called the Client Computing and Physical AI Group, where revenue slipped 5% to $8.1 billion.

The trouble lay in what Intel said about the next three months. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and adjusted earnings of 25 cents a share, whereas analysts had been looking for about $17.1 billion and 43 cents. In addition, adjusted gross margin is expected to fall back to around 38%, which would undo much of the progress the third quarter had just shown.

Two problems sit behind that weaker outlook. The first is the PC market, which Intel expects to keep shrinking for some time. “We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year,” Zinsner said, and the company now expects PC shipments to fall by around 12% this year and by roughly 10% in 2027. AI data centres are absorbing a growing share of the world’s memory chips, which is pushing up the cost of laptops and desktops and, in turn, putting buyers off. Intel has also flagged industry-wide shortages of memory and chip substrates as a risk to its business.

title: Japan Gives Esports a Spot Next to Olympians at Its Sports Festival 2026
content:
Esports had its own corner at Japan’s Sports Festival 2026 in Tokyo on Tuesday 3 November, a free public event run by the country’s national sports bodies to celebrate the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games and Asian Para Games . The festival took place from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. local time at the Ajinomoto National Training Center East in Kita ward, one of the centers where Japan’s national team athletes train.

It was organised by the Japan Sports Agency , the Japan Sport Council , the Japan Sport Association, the Japanese Olympic Committee , the Japanese Para Sports Association and the Japan Recreation Association, with Ajinomoto as a cooperating partner. The event was a special edition of Japan’s annual Sports Day celebration, and this year it was held on Culture Day, a national holiday.

The esports experience ran as a free drop-in session from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., and visitors did not need to register in advance. Groups played racing, football and rhythm games for about five to ten minutes at a time. Some of the games used standard controllers, while others were motion-based, so players controlled them by moving their bodies. The organisers said the zone was open to everyone from children to adults, although they did not name the games or any esports partners. Children who took part in the afternoon session of the festival’s Active Child Program also got priority access.

The esports zone sat inside a full day of traditional sport. The festival opened with a ceremony and a group exercise led by Olympians and Paralympians, followed by a talk show in which athletes spoke about their sports and careers. Families could also tour the training centre, visit a memorial gallery for Aichi-Nagoya 2026 and try 20 recreational sports. Meanwhile, Olympic swimmer Takeshi Matsuda led a cooking class on what athletes eat, and a separate programme mixed sport with traditional Japanese arts to mark Culture Day.

The festival came about a month after the Aichi-Nagoya Games, where esports had 11 medal events across 13 games . Japan won gold in Pokémon UNITE by beating Indonesia in the final, and Kurihara Yuki won the Puyo Puyo Champions event. However, Japan had to settle for silver in Identity V after losing the final to China .

With that in mind, giving esports a space at a festival run by the Japan Sports Agency and the Japanese Olympic Committee suggests the country’s sports bodies now see gaming as part of the Asian Games legacy they want to carry forward. The format was small, and the games were chosen for families rather than competitive players, but it put esports on the same programme as Olympians, Paralympians and the national training centre itself.

title: Valve Locks In 32 Teams for PGL Major Singapore 2026, TYLOO and Fnatic miss out
content:
Valve has locked in all 32 teams for PGL Major Singapore 2026 . Every place came from the Valve Regional Standings published on 2 November, so there were no open qualifiers this time, and Stage 1 begins in Singapore on 24 November. MOUZ top the global standings with 1,960 points, ahead of Vitality on 1,922, FURIA on 1,912, Aurora on 1,860 and Spirit on 1,842.

Europe takes 18 of the 32 places, while the Americas get nine and Asia five. Moreover, the highest-ranked teams skip the early rounds altogether: eight sides go straight to Stage 3, eight more begin in Stage 2, and the remaining 16 have to start from Stage 1.

Six European teams, MOUZ, Vitality, Aurora, Spirit, BetBoom and Falcons, are invited directly to Stage 3 on 2 December, along with FURIA and Legacy from the Americas. Falcons arrive as the reigning Major champions after beating FURIA 3-0 at IEM Cologne in June, although they sit only seventh in the global list with 1,764 points. FURIA, on the other hand, come in on form after winning PGL Masters Bucharest against Nemiga last week. No Asian team ranked high enough for a Stage 3 invite.

Stage 2 begins on 28 November with FUT, Nemiga, G2, 1win, Natus Vincere and Astralis from Europe, MIBR from the Americas and The MongolZ, who are Asia’s highest-ranked team.

Stage 1, however, is where some of the biggest names have to begin. FaZe and Team Liquid both start there on 24 November, alongside Ninjas in Pyjamas, PARIVISION, HEROIC, Eternal Fire and 100 Thieves from Europe, and 9z, M80, DENDELE, Imperial and Wildcard from the Americas. Asia’s other four teams, BC.Game, FlyQuest, Chinggis Warriors and Lynn Vision, also start in Stage 1. Only the top eight of those 16 teams move on to Stage 2, so a poor few days could end a Major run before the top seeds have even played.

The race for the last places came down to a handful of points. 100 Thieves took Europe’s 18th and final spot with 1,511 points after winning FiRe Last Chance in Buenos Aires, which left them 23 points clear of HOTU and fnatic, who finished level on 1,488. Virtus.pro were further back in 23rd place in Europe. In the Americas, meanwhile, Wildcard claimed the ninth and last place with 1,391 points, while NRG were the first team out on 1,322.

title: VCT EMEA : la Karmine Corp prolonge ZE1SH jusqu’en 2028 (off.)
content:
La Karmine Corp tient son entraîneur pour les deux prochaines saisons. Le club de Kameto a annoncé la prolongation d’Ahmed « ZE1SH » Sheikh jusqu’en 2028, confirmant sa volonté de construire sur les bases posées cette année. Présent au sein de la structure depuis 2022, l’Égyptien a occupé plusieurs fonctions au fil des saisons, passant du rôle d’entraîneur adjoint à celui d’IGL, avant de prendre les commandes de l’équipe. Une fidélité récompensée après une année 2026 particulièrement mouvementée, mais finalement couronnée de succès.

L’histoire entre ZE1SH et la KC a connu plusieurs hauts et bas. En 2024, aux côtés d’Engh, il avait notamment participé au sacre de la Karmine Corp lors du VCT EMEA Kickoff, suivi d’une cinquième-sixième place aux Masters Madrid. Mais la dynamique s’était ensuite essoufflée, avec une saison 2025 très compliquée et un début d’année 2026 tout aussi décevant. Sa promotion au poste d’entraîneur principal, après le Stage 1, a finalement marqué un tournant décisif. Sous sa direction, les Français ont réalisé un parcours exceptionnel pour remporter le VCT EMEA Stage 2 et décrocher leur qualification aux Champions 2026 en tant que première tête de série européenne.

L’une des grandes forces de ZE1SH réside dans son approche particulièrement flexible du jeu. Plutôt que d’imposer des stratégies rigides et des enchaînements prédéfinis, l’entraîneur privilégie la liberté de décision et l’adaptation en cours de manche. Une philosophie qui a permis à la Karmine Corp de développer un style spectaculaire et imprévisible, tout en retrouvant les sommets de la scène européenne.

Malgré une élimination dès la phase de groupes des Champions 2026, la KC aborde désormais la saison 2027 avec de solides ambitions. Confirmée parmi les huit organisations partenaires du VCT EMEA pour les deux prochaines années, la structure française dispose d’une certaine stabilité pour préparer l’avenir. Cette prolongation constitue ainsi le premier mouvement majeur de son intersaison sur VALORANT. Reste désormais à connaître les contours de l’effectif qui accompagnera ZE1SH dans sa quête de nouveaux trophées.

title: Mahesh Babu Invests in Shortgun Games, the Mumbai Studio Behind Project Takedown
content:
Telugu film star Mahesh Babu has invested in Shortgun Games , a Mumbai studio that makes games only for PC and consoles. The studio announced on 3 November that he has joined as a strategic investor, however, the size of the investment has not been disclosed.

Shortgun Games was co-founded by Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta. Its main project is Project Takedown, which the studio describes as a high-budget, narrative-driven action adventure for PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, built to compete in North America, Europe and the UK as well as at home.

Mahesh Babu said India has “extraordinary creative potential” and that “the time is right to build original characters and cinematic worlds from here”. He said Chandan and Mehta’s plan to make PC and console games that match international studios was what drew him to the company.

Mehta said the studio was founded to “prove that India can engineer world-class interactive entertainment” for PC and consoles. Chandan said the backing would help Shortgun grow its technical team and hire more creative talent.

Shortgun brought in action director Vicky Arora, whose film credits include URI: The Surgical Strike, RRR and Tanaav, to lead the game’s action design. The studio says his team has handled motion-capture choreography, combat pre-visualisation and stunt work, which is then built straight into the game’s character animation.

The studio has been working towards a big PC and console release for at least two years. In July 2024, former members of the Rogue Heist team joined Shortgun to build a PC and console shooter, and the studio said it was looking to raise a $6.8 million seed round. Vicky Arora came on board as action director in July 2025, and a month later Shortgun was reported to have raised $1 million from angel investors for pre-production of a cinematic third-person shooter. Mahesh Babu’s investment now comes with Project Takedown named as the flagship game.

title: France Wants to Tax the Internet by the Gigabyte, Gamers Have the Most to Lose
content:
Only 35 of France’s 577 deputies took part when the National Assembly voted, shortly after 9 AM on Friday, the 30 October, to tax the internet by the gigabyte. The count was 11 for, 10 against and 14 abstentions. Amendment I-1358 to the 2027 budget would charge companies €0.055 for every gigabyte of data they send to homes and phones in France.

The measure is a long way from becoming law, and it may never even get there, the government and the budget’s general rapporteur both has opposed it. But it puts a price on the thing every online game, patch and esports stream is made of, and South Korea has already shown where that road can lead: Twitch left the country rather than keep paying for its traffic.

The Socialist amendment, led by deputy Laurent Lhardit, creates a taxe sur les producteurs de données numériques , a tax on producers of digital data. Internet providers would count how much data each sender delivers to their customers and report the totals to the tax office every quarter, supervised by the telecoms regulator Arcep. The text lets providers record who sent the data and how much of it, but never what it contained or where it went.

The bill goes to whoever sends the traffic. For content delivery networks, the companies that store other firms’ files on servers close to users, everything leaving their network counts. The tax is capped at 15% of the sender’s turnover in France or 2% of its worldwide turnover.

The government expects about €10 billion additional revenue a year. They cite an Arcep estimate that around 200 billion gigabytes reach French subscribers each year, and say Google, Meta, Amazon, Netflix and Akamai send about half of it. Arcep’s latest annual report backs up that concentration: those five accounted for 49% of the traffic relayed to French users at the end of 2025. Public accounts minister David Amiel disputed the €10 billion figure and argued that half of the money would come from smaller providers, many of them French.

TFT Set 19 will launch on Dec. 1 with patch 19.1. This music-themed set will then receive another update on Dec. 15 before the holiday season and the start of 2027.

The second BGMI International Cup ran from October 30 to November 1 at The Dome, SVP Indoor Stadium, with 16 teams (six from India, five each from South Korea and Japan) playing 18 matches for a ₹1 crore prize pool and two PUBG Mobile Global Championship (PMGC) 2026 tickets.

DRX won the first BMIC in 2025, NS RedForce won this one, and Korean teams filled the entire podium. Underneath that, though, three days at the Dome produced a lot more to talk about: an Indian side that held a PMGC slot until the final match.

I was in the stands at the Dome for all three days, so some of what follows comes from the seats as much as from the scoreboard.

These are the winners and losers of BMIC 2026.

This was never a title race. NS RedForce led after Day 1 with 72 points, led after Day 2 with 128, and walked into Match 18 with a 67-point cushion. They won that match anyway, a 21-point Chicken Dinner on Miramar, just to close it properly.

From where I sat, the moment NS RedForce sealed it was the strangest of the weekend. The Dome went almost completely silent. The champions had earned their moment, but this was a room full of Indian fans who had spent three days hoping for a different name on that trophy, and that silence said more about how much BMIC means to this crowd than any cheer could have.

title: Zeus refuse de prolonger avec HLE, un transfert XXL se prépare en LCK ?

Une manière de rappeler que le club espère toujours conserver son toplaner, même si la concurrence pourrait rapidement faire grimper les enchères.

À seulement 22 ans, Zeus possède déjà un palmarès qui en fait l’un des profils les plus attractifs de la scène internationale. Son éventuelle arrivée sur le marché des agents libres pourrait déclencher une véritable bataille entre les grandes organisations de LCK. Pour HLE, l’enjeu est donc considérable : parvenir à convaincre le Sud-Coréen de poursuivre l’aventure ou se retrouver contraint de reconstruire sa toplane. title: Worlds 2026 : les audiences s’effondrent, Riot Games face à un problème ?
content:
Les chiffres ne sont pas particulièrement rassurants pour Riot Games. Selon les données d’ Esports Charts , le Swiss Stage des Worlds 2026 a réuni en moyenne 1 008 817 spectateurs simultanés, soit une baisse de 4,9 % par rapport à l’année dernière. Le recul est encore plus marqué concernant le pic d’audience, qui s’établit à 1 836 125 spectateurs, contre environ 2,56 millions en 2025 et plus de 3 millions en 2024. Il s’agit tout simplement des plus faibles audiences enregistrées depuis l’introduction du format suisse en 2023, même si les chiffres restent supérieurs à ceux de 2022, dernière édition disputée avec une phase de groupes traditionnelle.

Sans surprise, T1 demeure l’un des principaux moteurs d’audience du tournoi. La rencontre entre les champions du monde en titre et Dplus KIA a été la plus suivie du Swiss Stage, avec 1 836 125 spectateurs simultanés. Derrière, l’élimination de G2 contre Hanwha Life (1 785 416) et le duel T1 – CTBC Flying Oyster (1 784 678) complètent le podium. Les confrontations T1 – KOI (1 736 719) et Bilibili Gaming – Hanwha Life (1 688 935) figurent également parmi les cinq matchs les plus populaires de cette première phase.

Cette baisse d’audience relance notamment le débat autour du Swiss Stage, introduit en 2023 pour remplacer les traditionnelles phases de groupes. Si ce système avait initialement permis de dynamiser la compétition, son fonctionnement fait aujourd’hui l’objet de critiques, notamment concernant l’importance du tirage au sort. Cette année, Hanwha Life a ainsi hérité d’un parcours particulièrement relevé, affrontant plusieurs équipes chinoises et coréennes ainsi que G2, tandis que T1 s’est qualifié sans remporter de rencontre contre une formation de LCK ou de LPL. Une différence de difficulté qui a notamment été soulignée par les commentateurs Jatt et Vedius.

L’organisation des Worlds en Amérique du Nord constitue une autre explication possible, avec des horaires parfois peu adaptés aux spectateurs européens et asiatiques. Difficile toutefois d’attribuer directement la baisse des audiences à ces facteurs. Malgré deux années consécutives de recul, les chiffres restent supérieurs à ceux de l’ancienne formule : en 2022, la phase de groupes avait attiré en moyenne 826 034 spectateurs, avec un pic de 1,39 million. Riot Games peut désormais espérer inverser la tendance avec les playoffs, qui débuteront le 3 novembre à Allen, au Texas, avec notamment un très attendu T1 – Karmine Corp en quarts de finale vendredi.

title: CS2 player numbers fall for eighth straight month
content:
October’s average is the lowest since February 2024, and no run of monthly declines in the game’s tracked history has lasted this long.

Counter-Strike 2 averaged 797,324 concurrent players on Steam in October, down 1.03% from September, according to SteamCharts . It is the eighth month in a row that the average has fallen, and the lowest monthly figure since February 2024, when it stood at 786,631.

The slide started straight after February, the high point of the year at 1,084,095. Since then the game has lost 286,770 players from its monthly average, or 26.5%. Compared with October 2025, the drop is 15.9%.

SteamCharts has tracked Counter-Strike on Steam since July 2012, and eight straight months of decline has not happened before in that data. The previous longest run was six months, from February to July 2021, in the CS:GO era. Before that, the average fell four months in a row in late 2017.

October’s drop of 8,314 players is the smallest of the eight. Most of the decline came in two months: April, when the average fell by 94,387, and July, when it fell by 63,422.

The peak tells a similar story. October topped out at 1,402,441, below September but above August’s 1,331,274, the lowest peak since January 2024. The all-time high of 1,818,368 is from March 2025.

title: DHL Brings Its Recruitment Drive to IEM Beijing After 50,000 Esports Applications
content:
DHL has taken its esports recruitment campaign to China. The logistics company is launching it at IEM Beijing 2026, the Counter-Strike 2 tournament running from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech·Biohyalux ECM Arena, and says the program has drawn more than 50,000 job applications worldwide since it began in 2022.

The campaign is run with ESL FACEIT Group (EFG), which organises IEM and has had DHL as its Official Logistics Partner since 2018. It uses esports content, social media and event activations to send fans to DHL career pages, where they can browse and apply for roles in operations, IT, engineering and student programs.

Beijing gives it a large new audience. DHL cites a Statista estimate of nearly 220 million esports users in China, along with EFG’s post-event surveys, which found that more than 75% of its Chinese fans are aged 18 to 29. ESL expects more than 45,000 fans over the week, its biggest standalone IEM in Asia, and TYLOO are the only Chinese team in the 16-team field. Our IEM Beijing 2026 guide has the teams, schedule and prize pool.

The program started small. In May 2022, DHL launched a Dota 2-themed careers page at the ESL One Stockholm Major, listing mostly IT jobs and tied to its role as ESL’s logistics partner, according to DHL’s announcement at the time . One listing let fans apply to be the assistant of DHL’s Dota brand ambassador, SirActionSlacks, with a chance to appear in one of his episodes.

By August 2024, when DHL and EFG extended their partnership for several more years , the recruitment campaigns had produced more than 10,000 applications. The same deal made DHL the logistics partner of the Snapdragon Pro Series mobile league and several DreamHack festivals.

The new figures show how far it has grown since then. DHL now runs the program across 21 hiring hubs in nine countries, using Counter-Strike, Dota 2 and Overwatch. It reports more than one million visits to its esports career platforms, over 400,000 job views and more than 50,000 applications. That is a five-fold rise in applications in a little over two years, and it works out to roughly one application for every eight job views, or one for every 20 visits.

The series also showed that Team Spirit’s success does not depend solely on their star carry. Their other players stepped up when it mattered, particularly Denis “Larl” Sigitov with his Earthshaker in Game 1 and Bohdan “Batyuk” Batiuk with Enigma in Game 2 and Timbersaw in Game 3.

“For sale is the official World Champion Trophy from the 2022 Pokémon World Championships in London,” the post reads. “I earned this trophy myself by taking 1st Place in Pokémon Unite the very first year the game was included in the World Championships.”

The trophy shows a Pikachu holding a smaller trophy while standing on top of a Poké Ball. Junglebook describes it as being in pristine condition and says it has only been held by him, during the 2022 awards ceremony. title: 1win deny HOTU in Moscow and put 100 Thieves in pole

Le mercato Rocket League continue de redistribuer les cartes au sommet de la scène européenne. Après les annonces de Gentle Mates, Vitality et de la Karmine Corp, Geekay Esports a dévoilé son nouvel effectif pour les RLCS 2027, composé d’Enzo « Seikoo » Grondein, Charles « juicy » Sabiani et Mathis « mtzr » Hoareau. Deux recrues particulièrement expérimentées qui rejoignent l’un des jeunes talents prometteurs de la scène française. L’objectif est clair : construire un projet capable de rivaliser avec les meilleures formations européennes, malgré une concurrence qui s’annonce particulièrement relevée.

Juicy arrive en provenance de la Karmine Corp, avec laquelle il a notamment remporté le Paris Major en 2026, tandis que Seikoo quitte Manchester City. Les deux Français avaient rapidement décidé de s’associer durant cette intersaison et envisageaient initialement de jouer avec M0nkey M00n. Mais le double champion du monde a finalement choisi de rejoindre la reconstruction de la KC, laissant une place disponible dans le trio. Geekay a alors saisi l’occasion pour réunir les deux joueurs autour de mtzr, qui poursuit sa progression après deux saisons de développement au plus haut niveau.

Autre annonce importante, Andy « Kassio » Landais fait son retour sur le circuit RLCS. L’ancien joueur professionnel, passé par les staffs de BDS et Vitality, avait décidé de prendre sa retraite d’entraîneur en 2025. Après une expérience auprès de la sélection marocaine dans le cadre de la FIFAe World Cup 2026, finalement reportée, le Français de 25 ans a choisi de retrouver la compétition. Il explique notamment avoir renoué avec sa passion pour Rocket League, une motivation qui l’a convaincu d’accepter ce nouveau défi.

Malgré ce recrutement ambitieux, Geekay Esports devra passer par les qualifications ouvertes européennes pour espérer participer au Club Kick-Off de Londres, prévu en décembre. Contrairement à plusieurs de ses concurrents, la structure n’a pas été retenue parmi les organisations partenaires du RLCS Club Championship 2027. Le nouveau trio français fera toutefois ses premiers pas en compétition dès le 2 novembre à l’occasion de la Coupe de France Slash 2026, où il pourrait notamment croiser la route de Gentle Mates, Vitality et la Karmine Corp. Un premier test intéressant pour une équipe qui espère rapidement bousculer la hiérarchie européenne.

title: Vico Opens Up About Mental Health Struggles After Career-Best Fortnite Year
content:
BIG’s Taylor-Petrik “vic0” Gatschelhofer, known to most fans as Vico, has opened up about years of mental health struggles, five weeks after finishing third at the FNCS Global Championship and stepping away from competitive Fortnite. In posts on X on Sunday, he said he attempted to take his own life shortly before Globals, and that he no longer has contact with his family.

Vico’s 2026 run with Malibuca is why BIG called them “the best duo of all time” after Globals. They won the FNCS Major 1 Summit in Düsseldorf , then took the inaugural Fortnite Reload Elite Series at the Esports World Cup 2026.

Globals, at the Lotto Arena in Antwerp from 24 to 27 September, nearly made it three. The BIG pair led by 32 points going into the final game and finished third , four points behind champions SwizzY and Pixie, for $160,000 from the $2,000,000 prize pool. Our Globals grand finals report covers how that last game unfolded.

BIG’s chief gaming officer, Roman Reinhardt, summed up the result at the time: “Third place at Fortnite Globals. So close, but that’s part of it and it stings. Not everyone can say they were one kill away from the Globals win.” He added a line aimed at his players: “We believe in you 100%.” The club’s own post on X put it more simply: “No third trophy but still a great result.”

In October, BIG announced that Vico was one of ten finalists for Esports PC Player of the Year at the Esports Awards 2026, with the winners due to be revealed in Miami on 17 November. “Vico has had an incredible year, and his journey is truly special,” Reinhardt said then. Vico called the nomination “a huge honour”.

The first sign that something was wrong came on the final day of Globals. Vico said he had almost not attended the event, a comment picked up and shared by community accounts within hours. That evening he announced a break on X : “will be taking a break from competetive fortnite for a while. dealing with a lot of private stuff outside my competetive carreer and want to focus on that first and figure my life out. Will be back next year.”

title: NOVA Esports Earn VCT China 2027 Spot With 3-0 Final Win
content:
NOVA Esports are back in VCT China. The organisation beat Unsettled Resentment 3-0 in the Week 2 grand final of the VCT 2026 China Threshold in Shanghai on 1 November, winning the second and final guest spot for the 2027 season. Unsettled Resentment never reached more than six rounds on a map: NOVA took Lotus 13-5, Abyss 13-5 and Split 13-6 .

It is a quick turnaround for a team that looked to be on the way out of the league. NOVA were one of four organisations reported to have been left off the 2027-28 partner list , alongside FunPlus Phoenix, Titan Esports Club and Wolves Esports. A week after losing one Threshold final, they won the other.

The Threshold ran over two weeks at THE HUB Performing Arts Center in Shanghai, from 21 October to 1 November, with each week’s winner taking a guest place in the 2027 league. Twelve teams entered, including former partners NOVA, FunPlus Phoenix, Titan, Wolves and Dragon Ranger Gaming.

NOVA’s first attempt came close. They beat Any Questions Gaming 2-1 in the Week 1 quarter-finals and KeepBest Gaming 2-0 in the semi-finals, then ran into Dragon Ranger Gaming in the grand final on 25 October. DRG won 3-0 , taking Summit 13-8, Split 13-3 and Lotus 13-9, and with it the first guest spot. DRG had swept their way there, beating Rare Atom 2-0, FunPlus Phoenix 2-1 and Titan 2-0 on the other side of the bracket. They had also been reported as missing out on partnership, so the win put them straight back into the league they were about to leave.

That left one place and a second week to fight for it. NOVA made the grand final again, and this time the opponent was Unsettled Resentment, who had beaten Octagonal Disposition Gaming 2-0 in Week 1 before going out to Titan 2-0 in the quarter-finals. The final itself was one-sided. NOVA held Unsettled Resentment to 16 rounds across three maps and closed the series without dropping a map.

The roster that won it is GuanG, swagzor, qiutiaN, Ezeir and cb. The players celebrated online soon after the final. For an organisation that was facing a year outside the top level, it means NOVA start 2027 in the league instead of outside it.

title: Test Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 sur PS5 : un retour aux fondamentaux qui fait du bien
content:
Chaque année, la sortie d’un nouveau Call of Duty suscite son lot d’attentes, de débats et de comparaisons avec les épisodes précédents. La série a beau rester une référence du FPS grand public, elle n’a pas toujours réussi à renouveler sa formule sans perdre une partie de son identité. Entre les déplacements toujours plus spectaculaires, les approches parfois très éloignées du champ de bataille traditionnel et les propositions qui privilégient la surenchère, j’avais parfois eu l’impression que la franchise cherchait davantage à se réinventer qu’à perfectionner ce qu’elle savait déjà faire. Avec Modern Warfare 4, Infinity Ward semble avoir pris une direction différente : revenir à un cadre militaire contemporain, à des affrontements plus lisibles et à une action nerveuse, sans pour autant renoncer aux sensations qui ont fait le succès de la licence.

Dès mes premières parties, j’ai apprécié cette volonté de retrouver un équilibre entre efficacité arcade et crédibilité visuelle. Les soldats restent rapides, les fusillades conservent leur intensité et les affrontements peuvent basculer en quelques secondes, mais les mouvements paraissent un peu plus mesurés. Les armes ont du poids, les déplacements gagnent en cohérence et les différentes possibilités offertes sur le terrain enrichissent les combats sans transformer chaque rencontre en concours de figures acrobatiques. Le résultat n’a rien d’un simulateur militaire pur et dur, et ce n’est d’ailleurs pas ce que je lui demande. Modern Warfare 4 cherche plutôt à proposer un FPS accessible, réactif et spectaculaire, avec une identité militaire suffisamment affirmée pour se distinguer de certaines orientations plus exubérantes de la série.

Cette direction constitue à mes yeux l’une des grandes réussites de cet épisode. Le jeu ne bouleverse pas tout ce que l’on connaît de Call of Duty, mais il retravaille plusieurs éléments importants pour donner davantage de cohérence à l’ensemble. Surtout, il ne repose pas uniquement sur sa campagne pour convaincre : entre le solo, le multijoueur classique et DMZ, j’ai découvert trois expériences qui partagent les mêmes fondations tout en proposant des objectifs et des sensations suffisamment différents. Cette générosité donne à Modern Warfare 4 une vraie valeur sur la durée et explique en grande partie mon enthousiasme.

C’est par sa campagne que Modern Warfare 4 cherche d’abord à marquer les esprits, et je dois reconnaître qu’Infinity Ward a plutôt bien préparé son retour. L’aventure nous entraîne au cœur d’un conflit international impliquant notamment les deux Corées et la Russie, avec des opérations qui nous conduisent dans plusieurs grandes villes et zones de combat. De Séoul à New York, en passant par d’autres environnements urbains particulièrement soignés, le jeu multiplie les changements de décor et les situations pour éviter que l’histoire ne s’enferme dans une succession de fusillades interchangeables.

La campagne adopte surtout une approche narrative intéressante en alternant plusieurs points de vue. D’un côté, nous découvrons le conflit à travers des soldats sud-coréens, parfois encore novices, qui se retrouvent plongés dans une guerre dépassant largement leur expérience. De l’autre, Captain Price suit une trajectoire plus personnelle, guidée par une volonté de vengeance qui l’amène à remettre en question certains principes ayant longtemps défini le personnage. Cette opposition entre des combattants confrontés brutalement à la réalité du terrain et un opérateur chevronné engagé dans une affaire intime donne au récit une dimension plus humaine qu’une simple succession de missions héroïques.

J’ai particulièrement apprécié les séquences qui prennent le temps de montrer les conséquences du conflit sur les populations civiles. Modern Warfare 4 ne se contente pas d’aligner des explosions et des interventions spectaculaires : il cherche aussi à faire ressentir la violence d’une guerre qui ne touche pas uniquement les soldats présents sur le front. Certaines missions, notamment du côté nord-coréen, adoptent un ton plus sombre et mettent en scène des situations difficiles, qui contrastent efficacement avec les opérations plus classiques menées par des unités d’élite. Cette diversité de points de vue permet de renouveler l’approche du récit et donne parfois aux événements une intensité qui dépasse le simple plaisir de l’action.

title: How to get Point Blank Kills in Modern Warfare 4
content:
There are some weapon camo challenges throughout Call of Duty history that give players the most trouble. In Modern Warfare 4 , several of these camo challenges have returned, including getting Point Blank Kills. These types of kills have long been a thorn in the side of camo grinders, but there are ways to make getting Point Blanks much easier in multiplayer.

Below, we’ll go through how to get Point Blank Kills and the best ways to go about doing so in Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer.

For starters, a Point Blank Kill is earned when you eliminate an enemy that is in extremely close proximity to you. It doesn’t matter when you damage an enemy, but when you see the kill pop up in the killfeed, you need to be within a certain range of the enemy for it to count as a Point Blank.

The exact range for a Point Blank Kill in Modern Warfare 4 is currently unknown, but we do know that it’s much closer than you might expect. In most cases, you need to be within roughly two meters of an enemy when you kill them to earn a Point Blank. This goes for all weapon classes as well, so unlike Longshot Kills , you have to be roughly two meters away even if you’re using something like a light machine gun or sniper rifle.

Now that you understand what a Point Blank Kill is, what’s the most optimal way to go about earning them in multiplayer? Well, it slightly depends on the gun you’re using, as some weapons are naturally stronger at closer ranges.

However, for the most part, you’ll want to use mobility attachments on your loadout so you can get your gun up quicker, which helps out tremendously when killing enemies at close-range. You could also go for an entirely hip-fire build and just shoot from the hip when killing enemies up close. This works best for most weapons, but you can ADS with something like an SMG or assault rifle and have the same results.

title: Call of Duty Passes $40 Billion in Lifetime Revenue With Modern Warfare 4 Launch
content:
Only a few days following the launch of Modern Warfare 4, the Call of Duty franchise has surpassed a whopping $40 billion USD in lifetime revenue, marking an incredible milestone for one of the most successful gaming series of all time.

The news came from Xbox CEO Asha Sharma herself, who confirmed this in an X announcement on October 26, shortly after the release of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. In case you missed it, MW4 came out on October 23 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2.

“One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40B in lifetime franchise revenue,” Sharma said in a statement. “An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us.”

One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40B in lifetime franchise revenue. An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us. pic.twitter.com/AlpXydEQIQ

The number goes on to prove just how far the series has grown, especially within the past few years. In 2020, Activision had confirmed that the lifetime sales for the franchise were hovering around the $27 billion mark. By 2022, it had passed $30 billion, with approximately 425 million units being sold. Data-based estimates in 2024 placed it at roughly $35 billion across game sales, microtransactions, and subscriptions.

This means that about $10 billion in revenue was added over the course of the past four years.

title: Nintendo Pulls SmileBASIC 4 as Tethered Switch 2 Jailbreak ns2jb Appears
content:

Nintendo appears to have removed SmileBASIC 4 from the eShop after a Switch 2 jailbreak surfaced, Nintendo Life reported.

Security researcher Sammy Hajhamid, who goes by pepsipu, built the exploit, called ns2jb, with help from OpenAI's Codex.

Readers following the wider Nintendo Switch scene should note that the exploit is far from a finished custom firmware.

The exploit lets arbitrary native code run on the console, without a hardware modchip.

title: How to Play Modern Warfare 4 Multiplayer Early With the New Zealand Trick
content:
You can play Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer early on console by switching your region to New Zealand. Console multiplayer unlocks at midnight local time on October 23, and New Zealand reaches midnight before anyone else, at 11:00 UTC on October 22. On the US East Coast, that works out to a 17-hour head start.

The trick works best on Xbox and through the Xbox app on PC. Steam and Battle.net players are out of luck because PC unlocks at one moment worldwide. PlayStation is possible, but it costs you a second account.

Console players get multiplayer at 12:00 AM local time on October 23. New Zealand has been on daylight saving time (NZDT, UTC+13) since late September, which is why its midnight lands at 11:00 UTC on October 22.

Some guides list the New Zealand unlock as 6:00 AM on October 21. That is wrong. The table below shows what time New Zealand’s unlock hits in your zone, and how many hours you gain over waiting for your own midnight.

The math favours the Americas. A player in Los Angeles can be ten matches deep before most of the US has even woken up.

title: Fortnite Wins Australian Court Battle, Reclaims Spot on iOS
content:
Fortnite returns to iOS in Australia on October 22, 2026, after the Federal Court of Australia ruled against Apple in the Epic Games antitrust case. Justice Jonathan Beach found that Apple broke competition law by limiting app distribution and payment options. Epic announced the return on X, and Apple plans to appeal. The court also ordered Apple to open iOS to third-party app stores and alternative payments by March 1, 2027.

This article covers the return date, the court ruling, the March 2027 changes, and Apple’s response.

Epic Games said on X that Fortnite would come back to the Australian App Store on Thursday, October 22. Players in Australia can now download the game straight from the App Store. Before this, they had to go through the Epic Games Store.

Big news: Fortnite is coming back to the App Store in Australia tomorrow! Today the Australia Federal Court told Apple to open up iOS after finding they violated competition law. Here’s what’s changing in Australia in March 2027: • iOS will be open to third party app stores •…

The return follows a ruling that Apple violated Australian competition law. The court found that Apple restricted how apps are distributed and how users pay inside them. It also ordered Apple to readmit Fortnite and other Epic apps once Epic sends a written request. Readmission stays subject to App Store rules that match the court’s orders.

Epic CEO Tim Sweeney reacted on X after the remedies were issued. He called the outcome a “huge victory for consumers and developers” and said Epic is studying the verdict. He added that more details will follow.

However, none are in high-threat areas, so you shouldn’t have a hard time getting there regardless of where you spawn.

Here’s a look at where each Police Station is located in DMZ:

Regardless of which Police Station you decide to enter, all you have to do once inside is find three containers to loot, which can be done by entering a few of the rooms in the main building. You’ll also need to eliminate five AI soldiers within the station walls. This is also fairly easy, as each Police Station is often crawling with enemies, both inside and outside.

And with that, you should have completed this DMZ Order on Page 5 in MW4 DMZ. If you’re still on this page, you’ll also want to check out our guide on where to open a safe in DMZ .

title: How to find and open a Safe in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
content:
Throughout your career in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ, you’ll continually get to complete DMZ Orders, which are specific tasks that earn you rewards the more you complete them. While some of the DMZ Orders are simple, others can be rather difficult, and one of the more challenging ones is to “Open a Safe.”

While this sounds trivial at first glance, you then realize that Safes aren’t too common to find on the Hajin map in DMZ. Luckily, though, we know of some dedicated spots for Safes that allow you to complete this DMZ Order with no problem at all.

For us, this specific DMZ Order was on Page 5, and it even says that you can find Safes in Compounds and Locked Spaces . Of course, that doesn’t help a lot, as you still need to go out and search for these locations and then locate the Safe itself.

While you might have some serious trouble trying to find a “Locked Space,” you shouldn’t have many problems locating a Compound. These are marked by a tent icon on your Tac-Map and are fairly common in Hajin, particularly out in the woodlands or the side roads in between the major points of interest on the map.

In order to open a Safe in a Compound, you need to enter it and then clear out 100% of the enemy AI from the area . This is tracked by a percentage meter that appears on the left side of your screen when you enter a Compound. There are usually around 10-12 enemies in each Compound, and when they’re all cleared out, your meter will read 100%.

From here, you need to find the Safe that the Compound has stashed. For the most part, the Safe is located at the top of the guard tower, which is found at most Compounds . Just climb the stairs to get to the top, and you’ll find the Safe sitting on the ground next to a desk. Interact with it, loot the contents, and you’ll get a mission completion for this DMZ Order.

Une séparation particulièrement symbolique pour une équipe qui s’était imposée comme l’une des références de la scène nord-américaine au cours des trois dernières années.

Après trois années passées ensemble, les deux stars américaines pourraient donc désormais se retrouver adversaires sur le circuit RLCS.
